newsitem.title: USA: USDA reviews ADM contracts, mulls debarment.
newsitem.headline: USDA reviews ADM contracts, mulls debarment.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department was compiling a list of contracts with Archer Daniels Midland Co as part of deciding whether to bar the agribusiness giant from federal programs, a spokesman said Tuesday.
No date was set for a decision nor was a figure available for the scope of USDA business with ADM, based in Decatur, Illinois.
ADM pleaded guilty on October 15 to two counts of price-fixing in food and feed additives. It must pay $100 million in fines.
Firms convicted of breaking federal law can be barred from doing business with the government.

In early October, USDA proposed to ban contracts with Sun-Diamond Growers of California following its conviction of illegal gratuities and campaign contributions. However, the debarment would not affect Sun-Diamond affiliates.

USDA agencies have been asked to report ADM involvement in federal programs, a spokesman said. Areas to be checked include the Food for Peace and Food for Progress programs, which donate or aid food sales overseas, and the school lunch and elderly-feeding progams domestically.
